sections.html:
The Register of Deeds sits on the first floor of the main courthouse at 301 W. Upton Avenue in Reed City, MI 49677. Call (231) 832-6113, fax (231) 832-6115, or write register@osceolacountymi.gov. The counter runs 9 to 5 on weekdays, holidays excepted, and the public computers shut off fifteen minutes early, at 4:45.

Reed City has been the county seat since 1927, and the register still holds books that go back to 1853. Beyond taking deeds, the office keeps a tract index for every parcel by legal description, and its register chairs the county Plat Board. Staff will not draft a deed or answer legal questions. A seller who needs a document prepared should hire an attorney or ask the title company at closing.

A deed costs a flat $30 to record, whether it runs one page or twenty. Cash, cards, checks and money orders are all accepted, with checks written to Register of Deeds. Card users pay an extra processing charge on top.

Osceola County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceCharge
Recording a deed or mortgage$30.00 flat
Releasing or assigning several instruments in one paper$3.00 for each beyond the first
Photocopy of a recorded paper$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 more
Plat copy$2.00 a page
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00 for five descriptions, then $0.20 each
Document sent by email$7.00
Staff name search$5.00 a name plus $0.50 a year
Staff search of the tract index$50.00 an hour

The treasurer's certificate fee rides along in the same payment to the register, so a closing agent writes one check for both.

The county publishes the combined rate as $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state. Behind those numbers sit MCL 207.504 (55 cents per $500) and MCL 207.525 ($3.75 per $500). A deed shows the sale price on its face, or an affidavit of value travels with it. If a sale bundles furnishings with the house, list the two values apart so only the real property is taxed.

Exemptions differ between the two taxes, and the state list is longer. Points that matter to Osceola sellers:

  • Family transfers from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild skip the state tax, with no matching county exemption.
  • Lender foreclosures and deeds in lieu are exempt from the state tax, and the county tax is exempt when the loan is government backed.
  • A price under $100 owes neither tax.
  • A court-ordered transfer owes neither tax unless the court sets a price.
  • A land contract owes nothing until title passes at final payment.

List any exemption on the face of the deed. The register at (231) 832-6113 can tell you how the office likes it phrased.

A short checklist from MCL 565.201 governs what the register can take, and a miss on any line can bounce the deed. Look for these:

  • Margins: a clear 2.5 inches at the top of page one, half an inch elsewhere.
  • Print: black ink, 10-point type or bigger, on white 20-pound paper that is letter or legal size.
  • Names: each signer printed below the signature and spelled like the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Addresses: the grantee's street address and the drafter's name and business address.
  • Privacy: the first five digits of any Social Security number removed.

Tax proof is its own hurdle. Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of land contracts need a certificate from the County Treasurer. Under MCL 211.135 the certificate covers liens and five years of paid taxes. A quitclaim without covenants of warranty skips it.

The county's online search covers 1988 forward, and images of every document can be called up by liber and page back to 1853. Handwritten grantor and grantee books run to 2003, and courthouse terminals show names from 1988. Browsing names is free.

Searching by legal description through the tract index costs $50 an hour, a rate the Board of Commissioners set, and staff do not do title or mineral searches. Mailed search requests get done as time allows, aiming for three days. If you need an answer the same day, call a title company.

The county's Fraud Notify service emails you when anything is recorded under your name. That helps an owner of a vacant, inherited or seasonal house spot a forged deed early. GIS parcel maps are linked from the same page.

sections.h2: What order to line up the paperwork
sections.html:
A sale in Osceola County moves faster when the courthouse steps happen in a sensible order. A seller working with a buyer from outside the area can hand this sequence to the closing agent:

  1. Pull the current deed from the online search or the public terminal in Reed City and check the legal description against the parcel map.
  2. Order the treasurer's certificate, because a warranty deed cannot be recorded without one.
  3. Have the deed drafted on compliant paper with the sale price or an affidavit of value.
  4. Work out the state and county transfer tax, and note any exemption on the face of the deed.
  5. Bring or mail one payment payable to Register of Deeds covering the $30 recording charge, the tax and the treasurer's fee.
  6. Sign up for Fraud Notify so that any later filing under your name reaches your inbox.

Each step is cheap on its own, and the Reed City counter handles most of them in a single visit.

Osceola County is a Northern Michigan county of rolling hills, with Evart and Reed City as the cities and Hersey, LeRoy, Marion and Tustin as villages. US 10 and US 131 are the main roads. The population is estimated at 23,516. The middle home value is $155,400, owner occupancy is 83.7%, and monthly rent is $807. No building permits were issued in 2025, so the housing supply is mostly older stock.

Ask the Osceola County Treasurer for a payoff figure before choosing a closing date, since a warranty deed will not record until the certificate is in hand. A cash buyer still needs the same deed, the same certificate and the same transfer tax payment, but skips the lender's timeline, so the paperwork above is often the only thing setting the closing date.

faqs.q: Is recording in Osceola County priced by the page?
faqs.a: No. The charge is $30 for the document, however many pages it has, with $3 more for each extra instrument a single paper releases or assigns.

faqs.q: Will Osceola County email a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Yes, for $7.00. Counter copies run $1.00 a page, and a certified copy adds $5.00.

faqs.q: Do I need a treasurer's certificate for a quitclaim deed in Osceola County?
faqs.a: Usually not. Warranty deeds and land contracts are the papers that need it, and MCL 211.135 excuses conveyances with no covenants of warranty.

faqs.q: Which Osceola County transfer tax exemptions help a seller?
faqs.a: A parent-to-child or grandparent-to-grandchild transfer skips the state tax, and a price under $100 owes neither tax. Write any exemption you claim on the face of the deed.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Osceola County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call (231) 832-6113 or email register@osceolacountymi.gov. The office is at 301 W. Upton Avenue in Reed City and keeps weekday hours.
